text:
sara: Auto-canary pause triggered for canary rollout 2026-03-runtime-kernel-merge. Canary at 10% got paused automatically — perf SLO breach on p99 latency. perf-bot reported spike: https://ci.internal/redwood/perf/98765 :exclamation:
perf-bot: ALERT: canary=2026-03-runtime-kernel-merge, metric=p99_latency, baseline=85ms, observed=142ms, window=5m, rate=2.7% > pause_threshold
raj: seeing same on the staging trace. quick summary: merge changed kernel selection heuristic to prefer fused-attn-v3 for seq<=512; fallback path seems to miss for some config causing KV cache misses and full re-encode on continuation requests.
eva: profiler flamegraph attached (short excerpt):
```
Hot functions:
 - fused_attn_v3_kernel (40%)
 - kv_cache_lookup (22%)
 - attention_rewrite_fallback (15%)
 - copy_kv_buffer (8%)
```
carol: stack from a failing request (p99 sample):
```
request id: r-44b
model: redwood-7b-q4
seq_len: 96 -> 256 (continued)
call path: runtime_dispatch -> select_kernel(v3) -> kv_cache_miss -> encode_full_seq
latency: 310ms
```
sara: thanks. two actions we should decide: 1) revert the merge that changed kernel selector, 2) push a hotfix that forces fallback to previous selector for canary until we fix KV behavior. Thoughts? :thinking_face:
raj: i ran a quick bisect locally. culprit commit looks like 0a3f9b2 (kernel-selector: prefer fused-attn-v3 for short sequences). bisect log:
```
$ git bisect start HEAD origin/main~10
$ git bisect bad               # HEAD
$ git bisect good abcdef12    # known good
Bisecting: 3 revisions left to test.
0a3f9b2 is the first bad commit
# 0a3f9b2 kernel-selector: prefer fused-attn-v3 for short sequences
```
eva: confirmed microbench on that commit shows 20% higher CPU for continuation paths with KV fragmented entries. The fused kernel has a different KV layout expectation.
perf-bot: CI regression link: https://ci.internal/redwood/perf/98765/diff - p99 latency jump introduced in pipeline job runtime-e2e-avg.
carol: deploy-bot, can you hold the rollback? We need to coordinate with infra for hotfix patch.
deploy-bot: Pause recorded for canary 2026-03-runtime-kernel-merge at ts=1768001123. No automated rollback because rollback-policy=manual for this release.
sara: hmm we set manual rollback for this one because it touched runtime selectors. Maybe change policy to auto-rollback on sustained >2% p99 breaches for 10m? raj: we should be careful — some transient noise causes flaps. My proposal: Gate parameters: if p99>target by >50ms AND affected request ratio >1% for 10 consecutive minutes -> auto-pause; if >2% affected for 15 minutes -> auto-rollback to last-known-good. Also require regression to be observed across at least two regions before rollback.
eva: that sounds reasonable. Also add a canary-level override to force legacy-kernel for continued traffic while we fix internal layout. Suggested hotfix config change (runtime config snippet):
```
# runtime config override
kernel_selector:
  strategy: region_pref
  overrides:
    canary-2026-03-runtime-kernel-merge:
      force_kernel: fused-attn-v2
      reason: 'temporary fallback until kv layout fix'
```
sara: +1 for hotfix fallback. Carol, can infra stage that to canary now?
carol: I'll push the override to canary namespace in 5m. prepping the change: `kubectl patch configmap runtime-kernel -n canary --patch '...'` and will monitor.
raj: short-term mitigation also: increase KV cache prob eviction window to reduce fragmentation: set kv.cache.fragmentation_threshold=0.3 -> 0.6. That should reduce cache churn for continuation requests.
eva: note: increasing fragmentation threshold may increase memory usage by ~8% on canary nodes. need to watch oom-kill.
sara: agreed. let's do hotfix fallback + kv threshold bump. If after 15m the canary still shows >2% p99 breach we will rollback commit 0a3f9b2. Plan recorded here.
perf-bot: ACTION: created perf-incident ticket PERF-3121, linked to commit 0a3f9b2 and canary run 98765.
carol: override applied to canary at ts=1768001187. monitoring dashboards: https://dashboards.internal/redwood/canary/98765
raj: initial numbers after override (5m): p50 18ms -> 17ms, p95 62ms -> 60ms, p99 140ms -> 90ms (big improvement for continuation traces), affected rate dropped 2.7% -> 0.4%
eva: profiler post-hotfix shows fused_attn_v3 kernel usage down and kv_cache_lookup restored typical hit-ratio.
sara: great. we'll keep canary at 10% for another 20m then resume rollout if stable. For follow-up: we need a test that simulates continuation-heavy KV fragmentation to catch this in CI. raj, can you add a regression test that forces KV fragmentation pattern?
raj: filing GH issue and test PR after lunch. Also adding a guardrail doc for rollout policy: will propose in eng-runtime on-call runbook.
carol: marking this thread resolved for now, will update if metrics move. :white_check_mark:
sara: thanks all. summary: revert candidate=0a3f9b2 if canary re-breaches >2% p99 for 15m; hotfix applied (force_kernel fused-attn-v2 + kv threshold bump). Follow-ups: regression test + rollout guardrail doc.
perf-bot: Incident PERF-3121 updated: status=mitigated, mitigations=[hotfix-fallback, kv-threshold-bump].
deploy-bot: Rollout resume scheduled at ts=1768002450 if no regressions.
carol: leaving extra logs here for postmortem: `/var/log/runtime/canary/98765/*.log` and summary stored in PERF-3121.
